assumptions: Success rate means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The current period is 18 Oct to 31 Oct 2026, compared with 4 Oct to 17 Oct 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. A sale and a data gap both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is flagged for context, not treated as a data error.
The success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 88.54%, order-level 90.89%, technical 92.11%. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure-code figures are per 100 attempts, so they are not directly comparable with raw counts.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% to 88.5% (203,741 successes out of 230,100 attempts, versus 148,791 out of 165,297). The drop is statistically significant.
By payment method, the change splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (about 68% of the drop) and a like-for-like rate effect of -0.47pp.

CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 10.9% of attempts while its own rate stayed about flat (81.7% to 81.6%). It contributed -0.62pp, almost all of it mix. UPI's share fell from 54.0% to 42.5% at a steady rate of about 93.0%, contributing -0.44pp.
NovaMart's share of attempts grew from 6.0% to 30.0%, and its own rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%. It accounts for -0.96pp (65%) of the total change, the largest of any merchant group.

Within payment methods, the biggest rate drop is Harbor Bank debit cards: 86.2% to 76.7% (down 9.44pp), worth -0.39pp of the overall change. Debit card as a whole fell 2.65pp, from 86.0% to 83.4%; no other payment method shows a significant change.
For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts (22 to 1,065 failures). Other failure codes moved by less than 0.4 per 100 attempts.
Harbor Bank debit daily success rates stayed between about 84% and 89% across the 4-15 Oct baseline days shown.
Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
Attempt volume rose from 165,297 to 230,100 between the two windows.
The drop depends on the definition used. In the current window, attempt-level success is 88.5%, order-level 90.9% and technical 92.1%.

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp, from 90.0% to 88.5%, over the last 14 days. About two-thirds of the fall (-1.00pp) is mix: more EMI traffic, which is weaker than UPI, and mostly from NovaMart's share growing from 6.0% to 30.0% of volume. The like-for-like (rate) effect is -0.47pp, concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards, where the rate fell 9.44pp.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check NovaMart's campaign calendar and compare its payment-method mix between the two windows.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's share jumped from 6.0% to 30.0% at the same time as CARD_EMI's share rose from 2.9% to 10.9%, and volume was about 39% above the usual level from 18 Oct. Electronics' share also doubled (10.6% to 20.5%).
hypotheses.text: A sale or campaign led by NovaMart, with a push on EMI and electronics, drove the mix shift toward lower-success EMI traffic.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk rules or thresholds changed around 18 Oct, and look at the daily Harbor Bank debit rate and risk-decline code to date the start of the shift.
hypotheses.rationale: Almost the whole rise in Harbor Bank debit failures is one risk-decline code (0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts) while technical and customer drop-off codes barely moved, pointing to an issuer-side decision rather than an outage.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules or fraud scoring on debit cards, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break NovaMart's success rate down by payment method and issuer for both windows.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's rate fell 3.8pp (90.0% to 86.2%) while its volume share quintupled, and the weak segments (EMI at about 82%, Harbor debit at 76.7%) are the ones that grew or dropped.
hypotheses.text: NovaMart's own rate fell because its traffic includes more EMI and Harbor Bank debit attempts, not because its checkout got worse.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules or fraud scoring on debit cards, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.
recommendations.rationale: This is the single largest like-for-like decline (-9.44pp), and its failures are concentrated in one risk code.
recommendations.text: Raise the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike on Harbor Bank debit cards with Harbor Bank and ask for the rule or threshold change and a rollback or whitelisting path.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A sale or campaign led by NovaMart, with a push on EMI and electronics, drove the mix shift toward lower-success EMI traffic.
recommendations.rationale: Mix explains about two-thirds of the drop, so headline success rate will keep moving with campaign traffic even if nothing is broken.
recommendations.text: Confirm the NovaMart campaign and EMI push with the merchant team, and report NovaMart and EMI success separately so planned mix shifts are not read as a performance decline.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
recommendations.rationale: Both codes rose across all traffic (EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE 0.14 to 0.50, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED 0.66 to 1.08 per 100 attempts) and are partly addressable on the merchant and checkout side.
recommendations.text: Investigate the rise in EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE and AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED, for example EMI eligibility messaging up front and the 3DS flow on higher-volume merchants.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: By payment method, the change splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (about 68% of the drop) and a like-for-like rate effect of -0.47pp.
recommendations.rationale: This separates genuine performance changes from traffic-mix changes.
recommendations.text: Track success rate with a fixed payment-method mix, or by segment, alongside the headline number during sale periods.
